text:
maria: Quick heads-up — I ran a quant sweep for gpt-lite-v2 on A100 (seq512). High-level: int4 gives ~2.0x throughput at batch8 but we see a latency regression at batch1 (~+12% vs fp16) and eval PPL up ~4.5%. FP8 looks like the best quality/speed tradeoff (x1.6 throughput, PPL +1.1%). Anyone else see the batch1 latency regression locally?

lee: Which branch/commit? I can repro locally on h100 and a100.

maria: branch: quant/optimize-kernels (PR #432). Bench command I used: ```./bench --model gpt-lite-v2 --quant int4 --batch 1 --seq 512 --profile --gpu a100``` Also ran batch8 same job.

bench-bot: queued bench job 9876 (quant/optimize-kernels) — ETA ~22m. /artifacts/9876 assigned.

devon: Noted similar patterns in my small tests — int4 seems to have higher kernel launch overhead for small batches. Also saw some quality collapse on long-context prompts (some examples in eval set show token repetition). Could be KV packing differences.

ash: (oops) meant to say ash: I'd propose a conservative canary: FP8 default for seq>256, int4 for short contexts where throughput matters. We should also run a focused quality eval on our regression suite.

lee: 👍 I'll run the bench matrix across a100/h100/t4 and with and w/o our kernel fusion patch.

maria: Eval set link: https://internal/bench/evals/quant-tradeoff-2026-03 — includes PPL, Rouge, and a few user-facing prompt checks.

devon: If it's kernel-launch overhead, try toggling kernel_fusion=true in runtime config — that fused path reduced latency for other quant ops in the past.

maria: Good call. I'll re-run with kernel_fusion=true. Starting a run now.

bench-bot: job 9876 finished. Summary: batch1 latency: int4 +11.8% vs fp16; FP8 +2.3% vs fp16. Throughput @batch8: int4 x2.05, FP8 x1.60. Quality: int4 PPL +4.5%, FP8 PPL +1.1%. Full logs: /artifacts/9876/logs, metrics: /artifacts/9876/metrics.json

devon: I'll kick off kernel_fusion run (job 9880) against the same hardware and eval set.

ash: ash: For canary safety, let's add automatic rollback if validation PPL > baseline * 1.03 OR tail latency > baseline + 15ms. We should also gate deployment by rollout% and error budget.

lee: Agreed on rollback guards. Also add a quick smoke test: 50 user prompts from prod-weighted distribution.

bench-bot: job 9880 queued (kernel_fusion toggled). ETA ~18m.

maria: Thanks — if kernel_fusion closes the gap we can keep int4 as the default for dedicated short-context workloads. Otherwise FP8 fallback for low-latency paths. I'll draft a rollout plan.

bench-bot: job 9880 finished. kernel_fusion results: batch1 int4 latency improved by 9.6% relative to the previous int4 run (now ~+2.2% vs fp16). Throughput and quality unchanged. Artifacts: /artifacts/9880/{logs,metrics,profiles}.

maria: Nice — fusion recovered most of the overhead. Devon, can you sanity check the eval artifacts and confirm the quality regressions are within our tolerances?

devon: Scanning — PPL delta on the regression suite is now ~+1.3% for int4 with fusion. The few prompt failure cases look more like tokenization edge-cases than quant noise. I think we're within the 1.5% guard if we keep a short-context-only policy.

ash: ash: I'll open the canary PR: runtime default: int4 when seq <= 256 && kernel_fusion=true; fallback to FP8 otherwise. Add rollout: 5% dedicated, smoke test + PPL guard + tail-latency guard. Tagging reviewers @lee @maria.

lee: I'll review the PR later this afternoon. If we get +2% latency delta at batch1 still, it's acceptable given the throughput gains for batch workloads, as long as the canary and rollback work.

maria: Perfect. I'll schedule the canary for the 2nd deploy window tomorrow. Thanks team :rocket:

bench-bot: artifacts/9880 profiler snapshot uploaded: /artifacts/9880/profiles/kernel_fusion_snapshot.pb

maria: Adding a follow-up action: I'll log a quick runbook step for ops describing how to flip fallback in case the canary trips the PPL guard. Will post the PR link when ready.

lee: 👍 good plan.

ash: ash: Thanks all — great teamwork on narrowing the perf/quality tradeoffs.
